title: My Morning
body: I get up at six every morning. First, I open the window and drink a glass of water. Then I make coffee and read the news on my phone. I like quiet mornings, because I can think about my day. At seven, I have breakfast with my family. We eat bread, eggs and fruit. After breakfast, I study English for ten minutes. I say new words out loud and try to remember them. At eight, I leave home and walk to the station. It takes about fifteen minutes. On the way, I listen to an English story. It is a good start to the day.

questions.q: What does the writer do first in the morning?
options: Opens the window and drinks water

questions.q: How does the writer go to the station?

title: A New Job
body: Ken started a new job last month. He works for a small company that sells kitchen tools. On his first day, he was very nervous. He did not know anyone, and the office was big and busy. His manager, Ms. Brown, showed him around and introduced him to the team. Everyone was friendly. One woman, Lisa, helped him with the computer system. At lunch, they ate together and talked about their favorite food. Now Ken feels much better. He still makes some mistakes, but he is learning every day. He thinks the job is hard but interesting.

questions.q: What does Ken's company sell?
How does Ken feel about the job now?

title: The Lost Umbrella
body: Yesterday it rained all day. In the evening, I took the train home. I was very tired, so I sat down and closed my eyes. When I got off the train, the rain had stopped. I walked home happily. At home, I suddenly remembered my umbrella. I had left it on the train! It was a blue umbrella, a present from my sister. This morning, I called the station. A kind man said, "We have a blue umbrella. Please come and get it." I was so glad. Next time, I will hold my umbrella in my hand.

questions.q: Why did the writer forget the umbrella?
Who gave the umbrella to the writer?

title: Weekend Plans
body: Mika and her friend Sam are talking about the weekend. Sam wants to go to the beach on Saturday. Mika likes the idea, but the weather report says it will be cold and windy. So they change the plan. On Saturday, they will visit a new museum in the city. It has a special show about space. On Sunday, Mika will stay home. She wants to clean her room and cook a big meal for her parents. Sam will play football with his team in the afternoon. They both feel that a good weekend needs some fun and some rest.

questions.q: Why did they change the plan for Saturday?
options: The weather will be cold and windy

questions.q: What will Mika do on Sunday?

title: At the Coffee Shop
body: "Good morning. What can I get for you?" asked the young man at the counter. "A small coffee, please," said Emma. "Hot or iced?" "Hot, please. And could I have a piece of that cake?" "Of course. For here or to go?" "For here." "That will be six dollars." Emma paid with her card and sat by the window. The shop was warm and the music was soft. She opened her notebook and started to write a plan for her week. Coffee shops help her to think clearly. When she finished, she said "Thank you" to the young man and left with a smile.

questions.q: What did Emma order?
What did Emma do in the shop?
options: She wrote a plan for her week

title: Learning a Little Every Day
body: Tom wanted to learn the guitar. At first, he practiced for three hours every Sunday. But on Monday, he forgot most of it. He felt bad and almost stopped. Then his teacher gave him some advice: "Play for twenty minutes every day." Tom did not believe it would work, but he tried it. After one month, he could play three songs. After three months, he played at his friend's party. Everyone was surprised. Tom learned an important thing. A little practice every day is better than a lot of practice once a week.

questions.q: What was Tom's problem at first?
What is the main idea of the story?

title: An Email to a New Client
body: Dear Mr. Lee, Thank you for your call yesterday. It was a pleasure to talk with you about your plans for the new shop. As we discussed, our company can design and build the shelves and counters you need. I have attached a simple plan and a price list. The total cost would be about twelve thousand dollars, and the work would take three weeks. If the plan looks good to you, we could meet next Tuesday or Wednesday to talk about the details. Please let me know which day is better for you. I look forward to working with you. Best regards, Anna Sato

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this email?
options: To say sorry for a mistake
To send a plan and set up a meeting

questions.q: How long would the work take?

title: A Short Team Meeting
body: Every Monday at nine, our team has a short meeting. It only lasts fifteen minutes, and we all stand up. Our leader, David, asks three questions. What did you finish last week? What will you do this week? Is anything stopping your work? Each person answers in one or two minutes. If someone has a problem, we do not try to solve it in the meeting. Instead, two or three people talk about it later. At first, I thought the meeting was too short. But now I like it. Everyone knows what the others are doing, and we do not waste time.

questions.q: How long does the meeting last?
What happens when someone has a problem?
options: The whole team solves it in the meeting
A few people talk about it later

title: Working from Home
body: Since last year, Yuki has worked from home three days a week. At first, she loved it. She did not need to take a crowded train, and she had more time for breakfast. But after a few months, she found some problems. She often worked late because there was no clear end to the day. She also felt lonely, because she could not chat with her co-workers. So Yuki made some rules for herself. She starts at nine and stops at six. She takes a walk at lunch. Once a week, she has a video call with a co-worker just to talk. Now she enjoys working from home again.

questions.q: What problem did Yuki have?
options: She worked late and felt lonely

questions.q: Which is one of Yuki's rules?

title: Giving a Presentation
body: Next Friday, Leo has to give his first presentation in English. He will talk to a group of customers about a new product. He is worried, because his English is not perfect. His friend Maria gave him some useful tips. First, keep the slides simple, with only a few words on each one. Second, practice out loud many times, and record yourself. Third, speak slowly and pause after important points. Finally, it is fine to make small mistakes. People care more about the message than about perfect grammar. Leo feels a little better now. He has started to practice every evening.

questions.q: Who will listen to Leo's presentation?
According to Maria, what do people care about most?

title: The Night Market
body: When I visited Taiwan last spring, my favorite place was a night market. It opened at six in the evening and stayed busy until midnight. There were hundreds of small stands selling food, clothes and toys. The air was full of smells: fried chicken, sweet potatoes, and a famous strong-smelling tofu. I was a little afraid of the tofu, but a friendly woman at the stand told me to try it. To my surprise, it was delicious. I also played a simple game and won a small toy. Walking through the bright, noisy market, I felt that I was really part of the city.

questions.q: When did the market open?
How did the writer feel about the tofu after trying it?

title: Why We Forget
body: Have you ever learned a new word and forgotten it the next day? This is very normal. More than a hundred years ago, a German scientist named Hermann Ebbinghaus studied memory. He found that we forget most new information within a day or two. But he also found good news. Each time we review the information, we forget it more slowly. So the best way to learn is to review new words several times, with longer and longer breaks between each review: after one day, then three days, then a week, and so on. Many language apps today use this simple idea.

questions.q: What did Ebbinghaus study?
What is the best way to remember new words, according to the text?
options: Study them once for a long time
Review them with longer and longer breaks
